title: Beef asado
intro: Beef brisket braised in soy sauce, brown sugar and star anise until it falls apart, then glazed with its reduced sauce. Sweet, salty and warmly spiced, it is lovely sliced over rice.

steps.text: Pat the beef dry. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches on all sides. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and sauté the onion and garlic in the same pot until soft.
Return the beef and add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, star anise, five-spice and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer until the beef is very tender, turning the pieces now and then. Add a splash of water if the liquid gets low.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce has reduced by about half.
Stir the cornstarch mixture, add it and simmer, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy. Remove the star anise.
Slice the beef or serve it in chunks, with the sauce spooned over rice.

tips: Hard-boiled eggs added for the last 15 minutes soak up the sauce and stretch the dish to feed a few more.

title: Beef curry
intro: Tender beef, potatoes and carrots in a mild, creamy coconut milk curry seasoned with fish sauce. It is the gentle, golden curry of Filipino home kitchens, made for pouring over rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the beef, pour in the water and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the potatoes, carrot and coconut milk and simmer, uncovered, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens.
Add the bell pepper and chilies and simmer until the pepper is just soft.
Season with the fish sauce, salt and pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Curry powders vary a lot in heat and saltiness. Start with 2 tablespoons, taste after the coconut milk goes in, and add more if you want a stronger curry.

title: Beef stroganoff
intro: Strips of beef and mushrooms in a creamy sauce made with all-purpose cream, the way Filipino home cooks make it. Rich and mild, it is served over rice or buttered noodles.

steps.text: Season the beef with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned but still pink inside. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and melt the butter. Sauté the onion until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and it evaporates.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the broth and Worcestershire sauce, stirring, and simmer until slightly thickened.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream and return the beef with its juices. Heat gently until the sauce is hot, without letting it boil.
Taste for salt and pepper, scatter the parsley over and serve over rice or noodles.

tips: Keep the beef pink when you first sear it: it finishes cooking in the sauce, and overcooked sirloin turns chewy.

title: Beef liver steak
intro: Slices of beef liver cooked bistek-style in soy sauce and calamansi with plenty of onion rings. Quick-seared so it stays tender, with a salty, tangy sauce for rice.

steps.text: Rinse the liver slices and pat them dry. Toss with the soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic and pepper and let them sit.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the onion rings until just softened and set aside.
Lift the liver from the marinade and keep the marinade. Add the remaining oil and sear the liver in a single layer, about 1 minute per side, until browned outside and barely pink inside. Set aside.
Pour the marinade, water and sugar into the pan and boil until slightly reduced.
Return the liver and onions and toss in the sauce for 1 minute. Serve right away with rice.

tips: Liver turns grainy and hard when overcooked. Take it off the heat while it is still a little pink in the middle; it finishes cooking in the sauce.

title: Garlic pepper beef
intro: Thin slices of beef seared with lots of garlic and black pepper, smothered in a buttery mushroom gravy and topped with crisp fried garlic. Peppery, savory and rich, it is made for pouring over a mound of rice.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, pepper, cornstarch and a third of the garlic. Let it sit.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat and fry another third of the garlic, stirring, until pale gold. Lift it out onto a paper towel and keep the oil in the pan.
Turn the heat to high and sear the beef in batches in the garlic oil until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same pan and sauté the remaining garlic and the mushrooms until the mushrooms are lightly browned.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the broth, add the pepper and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Return the beef with its juices and simmer for 1 minute so it soaks up the gravy. Taste for salt.
Serve over rice, topped with the fried garlic.

tips: Be generous with the pepper, as that bite is the point of the dish. Add the fried garlic only at the table so it stays crisp.

title: Pindang damulag
intro: Thin slices of carabao meat cured with sugar, salt, garlic and annatto, then simmered and fried until sticky and caramelized. Sweet, salty and chewy, it is eaten with rice and sliced tomatoes.

items.name: carabao meat
items.note: or beef round, sliced 3 mm thick across the grain

steps.text: Mix the sugar, salt, garlic, pepper and annatto powder in a bowl. Add the meat and rub the cure into every slice.
Pack the slices into a container, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 day, turning them once.
Put a single layer of slices in a wide pan with the water. Simmer over medium heat until the water evaporates and the meat is tender.
Add the oil and fry the slices, turning often, until the sugar caramelizes and the edges darken. Watch closely, as the sugar burns quickly. Repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with rice and sliced tomatoes.

tips: Cure for 1 to 3 days in the fridge. Freeze cured slices in meal-size packs and cook them straight from frozen with a little more water.

title: Balbacua
intro: Oxtail and beef feet simmered for hours with ginger, lemongrass and star anise until the broth turns thick and sticky, then finished with peanut butter, annatto and chilies. Rich and gelatinous, it is a hearty ulam best eaten with rice.

items.name: oxtail and beef feet
items.note: cut into pieces by the butcher

items.name: stalks lemongrass
items.note: bruised and tied in a knot

steps.text: Put the oxtail and beef feet in a large pot, cover with water and boil for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the meat and clean the pot.

Return the meat to the pot with the 3 liters of water, ginger, lemongrass, star anise and the quartered onion. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer until the skin and tendons are very soft. Top up with hot water to keep the meat covered.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté the garlic, chopped onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes break down. Add this to the pot.
Stir in the peanut butter, annatto, fish sauce and pepper. Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then so it does not stick, until the broth is thick and the meat slips off the bone.
Remove the lemongrass and star anise. Add the chilies and simmer until they soften.
Taste for fish sauce, scatter the spring onion over and serve hot with rice.

tips: In a pressure cooker, the long simmer takes about 1 hour. The broth sets like jelly in the fridge; reheat it gently with a splash of water.

title: Beef binagoongan
intro: Tender beef simmered, then cooked down with sautéed shrimp paste, tomatoes and a splash of vinegar, served with fried eggplant. Salty, savory and a little sweet, it needs nothing more than rice.

steps.text: Put the beef and water in a pot, bring to a boil and skim. Cover, lower the heat and simmer until tender. Keep 1 cup of the broth.
While the beef simmers, heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a pan and fry the eggplant until golden and soft. Drain on paper towels.
Heat the remaining oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Sauté the garlic, onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Add the drained beef and fry for 3 minutes, then stir in the shrimp paste and cook for 2 minutes more.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil without stirring.
Add the reserved broth and sugar and simmer, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef.
Add the chilies and fried eggplant and simmer 2 minutes more. Season with pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Brands of bagoong vary in saltiness. Add two thirds first, taste after simmering, and stir in the rest only if it needs it.

title: Ginataang baka
intro: Beef simmered until tender, then cooked in coconut milk with ginger, shrimp paste and plenty of chilies. Creamy, savory and spicy, it is a rich ulam for rice.

steps.text: Put the beef and water in a pot, bring to a boil and skim. Cover, lower the heat and simmer until tender. Keep 1 cup of the broth.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add the drained beef, the coconut milk and the reserved broth. Simmer uncovered, stirring often, until the sauce has reduced by about a third.
Stir in the shrimp paste, coconut cream and both kinds of chili. Simmer until the sauce is thick and a little oil rises to the top.
Season with the fish sauce and serve hot with rice.

tips: Stir often once the coconut milk is in, and keep it at a gentle simmer so it does not curdle or catch on the bottom.

title: Beef kulma
intro: A Tausug beef stew in a thick sauce of coconut milk, peanut butter and tomato paste, warmed with curry powder, cumin and lemongrass. It tastes somewhere between a curry and kare-kare, and it is a dish for celebrations such as Eid.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and sauté the onion, garlic, ginger and lemongrass until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder and cumin for 1 minute, then return the beef and pour in the water.
Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer until the beef is tender.
Stir in the tomato paste, peanut butter and coconut milk until smooth. Add the carrot and simmer, uncovered and stirring often, until the carrot is tender and the sauce is thick.
Add the bell pepper and simmer until just soft. Remove the lemongrass and season with salt.
Scatter the cilantro over and serve with rice.

tips: Peanut butter makes the sauce catch easily, so stir from the bottom once it goes in. Unsweetened peanut butter gives a more savory sauce.

title: Beef rendang
intro: Beef slowly cooked in coconut milk with a paste of shallots, ginger, turmeric and chilies, then thickened with toasted grated coconut. The Maranao-style version is spiced and fragrant, and saucier than the dry rendang of Indonesia.

steps.text: Blend or pound the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and chilies with the water into a smooth paste.
Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until deep golden brown. Pound or grind it to an oily paste and set aside.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the spice paste, stirring, until it darkens and smells sweet and the oil starts to separate.
Add the beef and lemongrass and stir to coat. Pour in the coconut milk and water and bring to a gentle boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring every 10 minutes or so, until the beef is tender and the sauce has reduced by half.
Stir in the toasted coconut paste, sugar and salt. Keep simmering, stirring more often, until the sauce is thick, brown and clings to the beef.
Remove the lemongrass, taste for salt and serve with rice.

tips: Toasting the coconut slowly is what gives rendang its nutty depth. It goes from golden to burnt in seconds, so do not walk away from the pan.

title: Beef with kailan
intro: Blanched kailan (Chinese broccoli) topped with stir-fried beef in a ginger and oyster sauce gravy. The greens stay crisp and slightly bitter under the savory sauce.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, cornstarch and oil and let it rest. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the salt and 1 tablespoon oil. Blanch the kailan until the stems are just tender and bright green. Drain and arrange on a platter.
Heat the 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef in a single layer until browned. Push it to the side.
Add the garlic and ginger to the cleared space and fry for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and toss with the beef until thick and glossy.
Spoon the beef and sauce over the kailan and serve right away with rice.

tips: The oil in the blanching water keeps the kailan glossy and green. Peel the thickest stems with a vegetable peeler so they cook as fast as the leaves.

title: Beef with ginger and spring onions
intro: Tender beef stir-fried with a generous amount of ginger and a whole bunch of spring onions. Fragrant, peppery and lightly savory, it is a quick Chinese-style ulam for rice.

items.name: stalks spring onion
items.note: cut into 5 cm lengths, white and green parts separated

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, cornstarch and oil and let it rest. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef in a single layer until browned outside and still pink inside. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and fry the ginger until its edges turn golden, then add the garlic and the white parts of the spring onions.
Return the beef, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until it thickens, then add the green parts of the spring onions and toss until just wilted.
Serve right away with steamed rice.

tips: Use young ginger if you can find it: it is juicier and milder, so you can eat the slices along with the beef.

title: Filipino beef barbecue
intro: Thin slices of beef marinated in soy sauce, calamansi, banana ketchup and sugar, threaded onto skewers and grilled with a sticky glaze. Sweet, smoky and tangy, like the classic pork barbecue but with beef.

items.name: beef sirloin
items.note: sliced 5 mm thick into 4 cm pieces

steps.text: Mix the soy sauce, calamansi juice, banana ketchup, sugar, garlic and pepper in a bowl. Before adding the beef, set aside 0.5 cup of the marinade for basting.
Add the beef to the rest of the marinade, mix well, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Thread 4 or 5 slices onto each soaked skewer, bunching them slightly. Stir the reserved marinade with the banana ketchup and oil for the basting sauce.
Prepare a charcoal grill for medium-high heat, or heat a grill pan.
Grill the skewers in batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side, brushing with the basting sauce each time you turn them, until cooked through and charred at the edges.
Serve hot with rice and spiced vinegar or more banana ketchup.

tips: Marinate overnight for the best flavor. The sugar burns easily, so keep the skewers moving and baste only in the last few turns if the fire is very hot.

title: Beef with tofu
intro: Golden fried tofu and thin slices of beef simmered together in a savory oyster sauce with spring onions. The tofu soaks up the sauce and stretches a little beef into a meal.

items.name: firm tofu (tokwa)
items.note: patted dry, cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu, turning, until golden on all sides. Drain on paper towels.
Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of the cornstarch. Stir the oyster sauce, remaining soy sauce, sugar, water and remaining cornstarch together in a bowl.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of oil. Sear the beef over high heat until browned, then push it aside and sauté the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the tofu, stir the sauce and pour it in. Simmer, tossing gently, until the sauce thickens and the tofu has absorbed some of it.
Toss in the spring onions and serve with rice.

tips: Press the tofu between paper towels under a plate for 10 minutes before cutting. Drier tofu fries crisper and spatters less.

title: Beef with cauliflower
intro: Beef slices and cauliflower florets with carrots in a light, savory oyster sauce gravy. Mild and saucy, it is an easy weeknight ulam that kids eat without fuss.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and sear the beef until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and sauté the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the carrot, cauliflower, oyster sauce and broth. Cover and simmer until the cauliflower is tender-crisp.
Return the beef, stir the cornstarch mixture and add it. Simmer, stirring, until the gravy thickens.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Cut the florets about the same size so they cook evenly, and slice the carrot thin so it is done when the cauliflower is.

title: Beef with asparagus
intro: Beef and crisp asparagus stir-fried with garlic and cracked black pepper in a light oyster sauce. Quick and savory, with the asparagus still snapping.

items.name: bunch asparagus
items.note: about 300 g, woody ends snapped off, cut into 5 cm pieces

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of the cornstarch. Stir the oyster sauce, pepper, water and remaining cornstarch together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the garlic and onion for 1 minute. Add the asparagus and a splash of water and stir-fry until bright green and tender-crisp.
Return the beef, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until thick and glossy.
Serve right away with steamed rice.

tips: Bend each spear near the base and it snaps where the woody part ends. Thin spears need only 2 minutes; thick ones can go 4.

title: Sizzling tenderloin tips
intro: Cubes of tenderloin seared and glazed in a sweet soy and garlic sauce with onions, served on a hissing hot plate with buttered corn. Savory, sweet and buttery, it is a steak-house favorite you can make at home.

steps.text: Mix the beef with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, garlic and pepper and let it marinate. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
If using sizzling plates, heat them directly over a gas burner on medium until very hot.
Meanwhile, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a small pan and cook the corn until heated through. Keep warm.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Lift the beef out of the marinade and sear it in batches until browned on all sides but still pink inside. Set aside.
Add the onion rings to the pan and cook until just softened. Pour in the sauce mixture and any leftover marinade and boil, stirring, until thick.
Return the beef, add 1 tablespoon of butter and toss to coat.
Rub the hot plates with the remaining butter, pile on the beef, onions and corn and serve while sizzling, with rice.

tips: No sizzling plate? A preheated cast-iron pan works the same way. Set it on a wooden board, never directly on the table.

title: Roast beef with gravy
intro: A garlic- and pepper-rubbed beef roast cooked until pink in the middle, sliced thin and served with a pan gravy made from the drippings. A centerpiece for Christmas and family celebrations, with rice or mashed potatoes.

items.name: beef top sirloin or rib-eye roast

steps.text: Take the beef out of the fridge an hour before roasting. Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Pat the beef dry. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic and oil and rub it all over the meat. Scatter the onions in a roasting pan and set the beef on top.
Roast for 20 minutes to brown the outside.
Lower the oven to 160°C (325°F) and roast until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 55°C (130°F) for medium-rare, about 50 to 60 minutes more.
Transfer the beef to a board, cover loosely with foil and let it rest.
Meanwhile, set the roasting pan over medium heat. Add the butter and stir in the flour, scraping up the onions and browned bits, for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth, then add the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce and any juices from the resting beef. Simmer until thick, then strain and season.
Slice the beef thinly against the grain and serve with the gravy.

tips: A meat thermometer is the only reliable way to get the doneness right. The roast rises about 5°C while it rests, so take it out a little early.

title: Beef meatballs in sweet and sour sauce
intro: Fried beef meatballs tossed in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with pineapple chunks and bell peppers. Sweet, tangy and a little salty, it is a crowd-pleaser for kids and handaan tables alike.

steps.text: Mix the ground beef, minced onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, soy sauce and pepper just until combined. Roll into balls about 3 cm across, then roll them in the cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the meatballs in batches, turning, until browned and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
In a bowl, stir together the pineapple juice from the can, banana ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and water.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry the onion and bell peppers over medium-high heat for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce mixture and bring to a boil without stirring for the first minute, so the vinegar mellows.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and add it, stirring until the sauce thickens. Add the pineapple and meatballs and toss until coated and heated through.
Serve with steamed rice.

tips: Wet your hands with water while rolling the meatballs so the mixture does not stick. Fried meatballs freeze well; sauce them on the day you serve.

title: Beef with pechay
intro: Thin slices of beef and bok choy stir-fried with lots of garlic and a splash of oyster sauce and sesame oil. Light, quick and savory, with tender leaves and crisp stems.

items.name: pechay (bok choy)
items.note: about 2 bunches, stems and leaves cut apart

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of the cornstarch. Stir the oyster sauce, water and remaining cornstarch together.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and fry the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the pechay stems and stir-fry until they turn translucent at the edges.
Add the leaves and stir-fry until just wilted.
Return the beef, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until it thickens, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve right away with rice.

tips: Wash pechay well: grit hides at the base of the stems. Dry it before cooking so the wok stays hot and the greens fry instead of steam.

title: Beef with green peppers
intro: Chinese-style beef stir-fried with green bell peppers, onion and ginger in a glossy oyster sauce. The peppers stay crisp and slightly sharp against the savory beef.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of the cornstarch. Stir the oyster sauce, sugar, water and remaining cornstarch together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add the onion and bell peppers and stir-fry until bright and just tender-crisp.
Return the beef, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss until thick and glossy.
Serve right away with steamed rice.

tips: Cut the peppers and onion to about the same size as the beef slices so everything cooks evenly and is easy to eat with rice.
